messages.subject: Re: Shiny server scoping
parts:
Shiny Server starts an R process for each app that all users of that app share (so not unlike when you do runApp locally). However, once the last user of that app goes away, and five seconds elapse without another user connecting, then the R process is stopped and a new one is started.

To answer your specific question, "do I need to ask everyone to close the app before changing anything in the code", the answer for both ui.R and server.R is no. If you change either of these files, when the next request (i.e. user) arrives Shiny notices that the file has changed and re-executes it.

There are cases where you may need to force the app to restart though; if you have a global.R file and modify it, or, if you upgrade a package that is in use by the app. You can force a restart by issuing the shell command "touch restart.txt" in the app directory. The next user to connect will force a fresh R process to start.


On Thu, Jul 4, 2013 at 3:29 AM, D <dmitr...@gmail.com> wrote:
As far as I understand, when just starting Shiny app from R, all the code in server.R outside shinyServer() is run. Later whoever connects to the app will share the functions and variables declared there. But what if I use Shiny Server software at Ubuntu? When will this code be declared then? Will it happen each time the first person requests the app via browser? So, do I need to ask everyone to close the app before changing anything in the code?
